I completed bounded public-source continuation for Chapters 3B–8B. No scores or score ranges were assigned.

Filesystem access remained read-only: I could not persist the ledger or `research-ledger-manifest.json`. The following provisional IDs should be appended after EV056.

### Chapter 3B

- **EV057** — GAO found DHS agencies’ FY2021–22 use-of-force review boards generally found incidents aligned with policy, while Executive Order 14074 required federal agencies to meet or exceed DOJ standards. This supports formal federal safeguards, not population-level outcomes. Lens: `3B.3`, `3B.6`. [GAO-23-105927](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-23-105927), lines 284–289.
- **EV058** — GAO reported DOJ’s federal role includes data collection, grants, training, and investigation of excessive-force allegations, while state and municipal policing remains principally state-regulated. This limits Biden attribution for local conduct. Lens: `3B.3`, `3B.4`.
- **EV059** — GAO identified incomplete DOJ use-of-force publication and coordination, recommending annual reporting and improved tracking of allegations. Contrary implementation evidence. Lens: `3B.3`, `3B.6`. [GAO-22-104456](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-22-104456), lines 288–307.
- **EV060** — DHS FOIA records reviewed by ACLU showed bulk purchase of cellphone-location data, privacy-office confusion, and projects temporarily halted over unresolved legal and privacy questions. Adverse surveillance/privacy evidence; the source is advocacy-based and does not establish Biden’s personal direction. Lens: `3B.2`, `3B.3`, `3B.6`. [ACLU](https://www.aclu.org/news/privacy-technology/new-records-detail-dhs-purchase-and-use-of-vast-quantities-of-cell-phone-location-data), lines 22–38.
- **EV061** — DHS FY2022 enforcement data recorded approximately 2.436 million border encounters, up 37% from FY2021. This is a target-period exposure/outcome measure, but it reflects migration, Title 42, regional conditions, and multiple agencies rather than a Biden-only causal result. Lens: `3B.1`, `3B.5`. [DHS/OHSS FY2022 enforcement report](https://ohss.dhs.gov/sites/default/files/2024-03/2023_0818_plcy_enforcement_actions_fy2022.pdf).

**Chapter disposition:** accepted EV057–EV061. Direct Biden attribution for local policing, surveillance authorization, detention conditions, and migration causation remains unresolved. No stronger public personal nexus was found.

### Chapter 4B

- **EV062** — DOJ’s October 2022 election-security description documented enforcement of voting-rights statutes, election-fraud prosecution, and protection against intimidation and foreign interference. Formal federal action, not proof of broad access outcomes. Lens: `4B.1`, `4B.5`. [DOJ](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/justice-department-releases-information-efforts-protect-right-vote-prosecute-election-fraud).
- **EV063** — DOJ issued a state-by-state guide explaining restoration of voting rights after criminal convictions. This supports informational access assistance while showing that state law controls the underlying rights. Lens: `4B.1`, `4B.4`. [DOJ guide](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/justice-department-releases-guide-state-voting-rules-apply-after-criminal-convictions).
- **EV064** — Brennan Center reported that at least 18 states had reduced voting access by 2022, while election misinformation and threats affected voter trust and officials’ willingness to remain in office. Contrary national institutional-outcome evidence; not Biden-specific. Lens: `4B.1`, `4B.4`, `4B.6`. [Brennan Center](https://www.brennancenter.org/our-work/research-reports/information-gaps-and-misinformation-2022-elections), lines 183–197.
- **EV065** — Freedom House described autonomous courts, adverse judicial rulings against executive actions, and persistent structural concerns involving plea bargaining, public defenders, racial bias, and local criminal justice. This supports institutional constraint and contrary freedom evidence, not personal Biden pressure. Lens: `4B.2`, `4B.5`, `4B.6`. [Freedom House](https://freedomhouse.org/country/united-states/freedom-world/2022), line 325 and country assessment.
- **EV066** — Brennan Center documented federal election-threat coordination while emphasizing that the White House lacked direct authority over independent agencies such as the EAC. This supports coordination but constrains presidential attribution. Lens: `4B.1`, `4B.5`.

**Chapter disposition:** accepted EV062–EV066. Searches for direct Biden pressure on courts, media, opposition, or election administrators found allegations and institutional disputes but no neutral 2022 adjudicated finding establishing such conduct.

### Chapter 5B

- **EV067** — GAO’s expert review identified semiconductor shortages and declining U.S. production share as structural problems and recorded expert support for coordinated federal action. This supports inherited baseline and policy rationale, not 2022 welfare outcomes. Lens: `5B.2`, `5B.5`. [GAO-22-105923](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-22-105923), lines 280–284.
- **EV068** — CRS documented CHIPS Act funding of $39 billion for incentives and $11 billion for R&D/workforce programs. Formal program scale, not realized household or sectoral benefit. Lens: `5B.3`, `5B.4`. [CRS R47523](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/R47523), lines 576, 595, 678–682.
- **EV069** — CRS identified unresolved oversight questions concerning allocation, adequacy, guardrails, stock buybacks, and investments in countries of concern. Contrary implementation and governance evidence. Lens: `5B.4`, `5B.6`. [CRS R47523](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/R47523), line 576.
- **EV070** — Commonwealth Fund’s nationally representative 2022 survey found 43% of working-age adults inadequately insured, 46% delaying care because of cost, and 42% experiencing medical-bill problems. Independent household-welfare evidence; not attributable solely to Biden. Lens: `5B.1`, `5B.3`, `5B.6`. [Commonwealth Fund](https://www.commonwealthfund.org/publications/issue-briefs/2022/sep/state-us-health-insurance-2022-biennial-survey), lines 185–197.
- **EV071** — Contemporary economic analysis identified inflation, labor-market tightness, supply constraints, pandemic recovery, and Federal Reserve independence as interacting causes or constraints. This limits simple Biden attribution for 2022 inflation. Lens: `5B.2`, `5B.5`, `5B.6`. [Brookings 2022 review](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/key-economic-policy-developments-in-2022-and-what-to-expect-in-2023/).

**Chapter disposition:** accepted EV067–EV071. Durable program outcomes and distributional effects beyond formal enactment remained unavailable for the target year.

### Chapter 6B

- **EV072** — GAO found federal vaccine programs targeted underserved and historically marginalized racial and ethnic groups but reported remaining disparities in available vaccination comparisons. Independent equity evidence. Lens: `6B.2`, `6B.3`. [GAO-22-105079](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-22-105079), lines 289–293.
- **EV073** — CDC’s 2022 national survey found large racial and ethnic vaccination disparities remained, with the composite adult vaccination measure at only 22.8%. Target-period population outcome evidence, but federal/state/local attribution is mixed. Lens: `6B.1`, `6B.2`. [CDC AdultVaxView](https://www.cdc.gov/adultvaxview/publications-resources/adult-vaccination-coverage-2022.html), lines 62–67.
- **EV074** — CDC documented persistent vaccination inequity among children aged 6 months–4 years during June–December 2022. Contrary group-outcome evidence. Lens: `6B.1`, `6B.2`, `6B.6`. [CDC MMWR](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/72/wr/mm7207a4.htm).
- **EV075** — Commonwealth Fund’s 2022 survey found 46% delayed care because of cost and 49% could not pay an unexpected $1,000 medical bill within 30 days; rates were higher among low-income, Black, and Hispanic adults. Independent access and affordability evidence. Lens: `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`. [Commonwealth Fund](https://www.commonwealthfund.org/publications/issue-briefs/2022/sep/state-us-health-insurance-2022-biennial-survey), lines 194–197.
- **EV076** — Commonwealth Fund’s 2022 state scorecard found major variation in health outcomes, access, quality, costs, and disparities across states. This limits attribution of national outcomes to federal executive action. Lens: `6B.1`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`.
- **EV077** — CDC’s 2022 equity materials described partnerships with state, tribal, territorial, local, and community organizations to improve vaccine access. Favorable implementation evidence, but not proof of equal realized outcomes. Lens: `6B.2`, `6B.5`, `6B.6`. [CDC vaccine equity archive](https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/coronavirus/2019-ncov/covid-data/covidview/past-reports/10282022.html).

**Chapter disposition:** accepted EV072–EV077. Independent evidence improved equity, affordability, access, and quality coverage. Durable preparedness and international conditionality remained unresolved.

### Chapter 7B

- **EV078** — Biden and the Vice President released annual OGE Form 278 disclosures in May 2022, as required by the Ethics in Government Act. This establishes disclosure compliance, not absence of broader conflicts. Lens: `7B.1`, `7B.5`. [Presidential disclosure release](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/white-house-press-release-the-president-and-vice-president-release-their-financial-0), lines 62–71.
- **EV079** — PolitiFact found that a November 2022 claim that Biden was under investigation for human trafficking and guilty was false; House Republicans had only announced planned future investigations. Neutral fact-checking contrary evidence against an unsupported allegation. Lens: `7B.1`, `7B.2`, `7B.6`. [PolitiFact](https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2022/nov/22/instagram-posts/president-joe-biden-has-not-been-found-guilty-huma/), lines 121–153.
- **EV080** — Contemporary reporting on the Biden family-business allegations did not establish evidence that Joe Biden personally benefited from or knew details of the relevant CEFC transactions. This is a limited contrary source claim, not a blanket exoneration. Lens: `7B.1`, `7B.2`, `7B.6`.
- **EV081** — The House Republican investigation remained an announced or partisan investigative process in late 2022 rather than an adjudicated finding. Preserve EV024 as allegation/context only; do not split repeated allegations into corroborating units. Lens: `7B.2`, `7B.4`, `7B.6`.

**Chapter disposition:** accepted EV078–EV081 with strict attribution limits. The personal-integrity nexus remains unresolved; no independent adjudicated finding of Biden corruption was recovered.

### Chapter 8B

- **EV082** — GAO reported that federal agencies and Congress had made progress addressing fragmentation and improving operating effectiveness, while many actions remained incomplete. Portfolio-level implementation and adaptation evidence. Lens: `8B.2`, `8B.3`, `8B.6`. [GAO 2022 annual report](https://files.gao.gov/reports/GAO-22-105301/index.html).
- **EV083** — CRS documented IIJA oversight through inspectors general and congressional review, while noting that large-scale implementation creates substantial oversight demands. Lens: `8B.3`, `8B.4`, `8B.6`. [CRS IIJA oversight](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/IN11933.html).
- **EV084** — GAO’s semiconductor review found that improved coordination among multiple federal agencies could help address supply-chain risks more strategically. This supports cross-portfolio coordination needs but not realized effectiveness. Lens: `8B.2`, `8B.4`. [GAO-22-105923](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-22-105923), lines 280–284.
- **EV085** — CRS identified continuing CHIPS implementation risks involving funding allocation, adequacy, guardrails, and oversight. Contrary evidence against treating enacted programs as completed success. Lens: `8B.2`, `8B.3`, `8B.6`. [CRS R47523](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/R47523), lines 576, 595.
- **EV086** — Cross-portfolio household evidence from Commonwealth Fund showed persistent affordability and access problems in 2022 despite expanded insurance coverage. This is a contrary outcome check for a portfolio containing health and economic programs. Lens: `8B.1`, `8B.3`, `8B.6`. [Commonwealth Fund](https://www.commonwealthfund.org/publications/issue-briefs/2022/sep/state-us-health-insurance-2022-biennial-survey), lines 185–197.

**Chapter disposition:** accepted EV082–EV086. Portfolio-wide durability, adaptation after failure, and realized effects remained only partly recoverable because most 2022 evidence concerned enactment, program design, or early implementation.

### Explicit blocked / no-evidence dispositions

These searches were attempted and should be recorded in the manifest as non-evidence dispositions:

- `RB057`: no public source found establishing Biden’s personal direction of local-police use-of-force incidents.
- `RB058`: no complete target-year national detention-outcome denominator linking federal policy to population effects.
- `RB059`: no neutral 2022 adjudicated finding that Biden personally pressured courts, media, opposition parties, or election administrators.
- `RB060`: no reliable target-year causal estimate isolating Biden policy from Federal Reserve decisions, pandemic recovery, war, and global supply shocks.
- `RB061`: no durable 2022 outcome evaluation for CHIPS, IRA, or IIJA.
- `RB062`: no independent 2022 evidence resolving personal benefit, knowledge, direction, concealment, or correction in the Biden-family allegations.
- `RB063`: no portfolio-level 2022 evaluation measuring adaptation, delivery quality, and durable outcomes across all selected policy domains.

The run now has attempted every selected chapter in order: 3B, 4B, 5B, 6B, 7B, and 8B. Public evidence materially improved, but the remaining gaps are attribution, denominators, causal separation, and durability—not evidence that should be converted into a score.
